headline: Senate Proposal Would Add Random Drug Tests and More Frequent Psych Reviews for Gun Owners
seoTitle: Senate Proposal Adds Random Drug Tests, Psych Reviews for Gun Owners | FMB News
seoDescription: A Senate firearms-reform proposal would add random drug testing, more frequent neuro-psychiatric review and faster license action for high-risk gun owners, building on existing screening requirements.
deck: The proposal would go beyond existing applicant screening by adding random testing and more frequent review, according to the approved FMB News morning brief.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: An approved FMB News morning brief reports that senators are pushing additional firearms safeguards that would include random drug testing, more frequent neuro-psychiatric review and quicker licensing action when a gun owner presents serious public-safety risks.
The brief attributes the proposal to senators and the Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs in the aftermath of recent school firearm incidents.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Current Philippine law already requires firearm-license applicants to pass a psychiatric test and a drug test. Republic Act No. 10591 sets those requirements for a License to Own and Possess Firearms, while Republic Act No. 9165 separately requires drug testing for applicants for firearm licenses and permits to carry firearms outside residence.

Because those safeguards already exist, the reported proposal is best understood as an expansion toward random or continuing testing, shorter review intervals and stronger red-flag mechanisms, not the first introduction of drug or psychiatric screening for gun ownership.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The policy debate centers on whether one-time or renewal-stage screening is enough to identify later changes in behavior, mental health, drug use or violence risk, and how far police authority should extend before a court finding or criminal conviction.
Any legislation would also have to balance public safety, due process, privacy and workable standards for when licenses may be suspended or firearms temporarily secured.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for an actual bill text, committee hearing notice or Senate legislative record specifying the proposed testing frequency, renewal period, appeal process and legal threshold for suspension or confiscation. Those details will determine how different the measure is from existing law.
